overall: The AG found violations for an insufficiently specific notice that omitted the town administrator as the subject of a Purpose 2 executive session and for a post-announcement open-session vote; it found no violation on termination-topic notice or deliberation, and declined to nullify the votes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the December 1 meeting notice was not specific enough about the executive session topic.
Complaint alleged the notice was deficient for omitting the possible termination of the town administrator as a listed topic.
allegations.key_passage: Although a close question, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by not including termination as a topic of discussion in the notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board voted in open session after the chair said it would reconvene only to adjourn.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Chair announced that the Board would reconvene in open session but only to adjourn, effectively depriving the public of the opportunity to decide whether to be present for any additional open session business.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair and one member, forming a quorum, deliberated about the administrator outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The evidence that we have reviewed is insufficient to find that the Board deliberated outside a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked the AG to nullify the December 1 votes terminating the town administrator.
allegations.key_passage: For all of these reasons, we decline to exercise our authority to nullify the December votes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
All Board members must attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar provided by the AG's office within 90 days of the letter and certify to the office that they have done so.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Additionally, in light of the Board's misunderstanding of multiple areas of the Open Meeting Law, as revealed by this Open Meeting Law complaint, we order all members of the Board to attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar provided by our office within 90 days of the date of this letter, and to certify to our office that they have done so.
